meta.note: Evidence records support editorial freshness dates. They do not replace the linked authority or a traveller's passport-specific confirmation.

reviews.evidence: SAPS confirms 10111 for police emergencies; South African government guidance confirms 10177 for ambulance and 112 for mobile emergencies.
NamPol confirms the countrywide police emergency line 10111. City of Windhoek confirms 061 211111 for ambulance, fire and rescue within the municipal boundary.
Botswana Police confirms 999; the Government of Botswana emergency medical service confirms ambulance 997. The police emergency directory also lists fire 998.
Zambia Police lists emergency 991, ambulance 992 and fire 993. The previous police number 999 was removed.
Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health Impilo service lists 999 for ambulance, police and fire, with 112 as the alternative emergency number. The previous service-specific numbers were removed.
Mozambique's official tourism information lists 112 and 122 for police/emergency contact. The previous 119/117 summary was removed.
Malawi's Ministry of Homeland Security lists police 997, fire 998 and ambulance 999. The previous summary incorrectly labelled 998 as ambulance.
The Government of Lesotho lists national emergency 112 and national ambulance 121. The unsubstantiated police number 123 was removed.
The Government of Eswatini lists police 999 and fire 933; its health emergency service confirms ambulance 977.
DHA guidance makes eligibility passport-specific and provides an ETA route for eligible travellers. Broad regional promises were replaced with a passport-dependent summary.

Namibia's official visa-on-arrival service and government fact sheet confirm the reciprocal regime introduced on 1 April 2025, including the N$1,600 standard adult fee for affected non-African passports.
Government guidance confirms nationality-based exemptions, six-month passport validity and a maximum 90-day visitor stay in a calendar year.
Zambia Immigration confirms three nationality categories, a visitor/tourist allowance up to 90 days in 12 months, and the USD 50 KAZA UniVisa for eligible trips.
Zimbabwe Immigration confirms the A/B/C regime: visa-free, visa obtainable at port of entry, and prior eVisa respectively. The previous summary did not distinguish these categories.

Zimbabwe's current regime shows the selected UK, US, Australian, Canadian and Indian profiles as visa-required but eligible at the port of entry; the EU grouping requires nationality-specific checking. Incorrect visa-free claims were removed.
Mozambique's new official portal distinguishes regional exemptions, a 30-day eTA list, the broader eVisa scheme and embassy-only passports. The former generic visa-on-arrival claim was removed.
The official eligibility table confirms 30-day eTA eligibility for UK, US and Canadian passports, eVisa eligibility for Australia and India, and 30-day exemption for ordinary South African passports.

Malawi's 2026 amendment requires visas except for the current exemption schedule. A notice effective 24 February 2026 allows Category Two nationals to use visa on arrival while Category One needs approval before departure; eVisa is recommended for eligible travellers.

The 2026 exemption schedule removed the former broad exemption for UK, US, EU, Australian and Canadian ordinary passports. The matrix now marks a visa action and sends travellers to the official eligibility wizard instead of promising visa on arrival across all profiles.
Lesotho Home Affairs says foreign visitors generally need the eVisa unless covered by a visa-abolition agreement or an eligible Commonwealth exemption.
Eswatini's official guidelines make the requirement nationality-specific and limit the visitor visa category to stays of no more than one month.
The FCDO destination advice and U.S. State Department advisory both resolve and identify South Africa. The retired U.S. country-information URL was replaced with its current advisory URL.

The FCDO destination advice and U.S. State Department advisory both resolve and identify Malawi. The retired U.S. country-information URL was replaced with its current advisory URL.

The FCDO destination advice resolves and identifies Lesotho. The State Department's new-style destination URL returned an error, so this record uses the functioning official advisory page dated 17 June 2026.
The FCDO destination advice and U.S. State Department advisory both resolve and identify Eswatini. The retired U.S. country-information URL was replaced with its current advisory URL.
SANParks' current 2025/26 page lists R602 international adult and R275 SADC adult daily conservation fees. The old R486/R243 values and generic homepage citation were replaced.

SANParks publishes separate fees by access point. Boulders is R245 and Cape Point R515 for international adults through 31 October 2026; the independently operated cableway was removed as the park headline price.
SANParks lists R492 international adult and R225 SADC adult daily conservation fees through 31 October 2026. The main entrance is listed as 07:00 to 19:00, with game-area times varying.

The latest official public MEFT schedule located lists N$150 per international adult, N$100 per SADC adult and N$50 for a vehicle with 10 seats or fewer. It took effect in 2021, so the card explicitly requires reconfirmation.

The latest official public MEFT schedule located lists N$150 per international adult, N$100 per SADC adult and N$50 for a small vehicle. The former N$142/N$80/N$30 figures were removed and gate times require NWR confirmation.
MEFT's public schedule covers Skeleton Coast fees, while access rules differ by section. The card now separates the published tariff from the need to confirm permits and route restrictions.

Botswana announced revised wildlife and park fees for 2026, but a dependable final public Category A tariff was not located. The unsupported P120/P60/P10 figures were withdrawn and travellers are directed to DWNP.

Botswana announced revised wildlife and park fees for 2026, but a dependable final public Category A tariff was not located. The unsupported P120/P60/P10 figures were withdrawn and travellers are directed to DWNP.

Botswana announced revised wildlife and park fees for 2026, but a dependable final public Category B tariff was not located. The unsupported P50/P30/P10 figures were withdrawn and travellers are directed to DWNP.

The latest published Zambia tourism-authority table located is labelled 2025 and lists $25 international entry, $30 for self-drivers, $20 resident/SADC and $15 for a foreign vehicle under three tons. The card preserves the year and requires DNPW confirmation.

The latest published Zambia tourism-authority table located is labelled 2025 and lists $20 international entry, $15 resident/SADC and $15 for a foreign vehicle under three tons. The vehicle and SADC figures were corrected and marked for reconfirmation.

The latest published Zambia tourism-authority table located is labelled 2025 and lists $25 international entry, $30 for self-drivers, $20 resident/SADC and $15 for a foreign vehicle. The old $20/$10 figures were corrected and marked for reconfirmation.
ZimParks' 2026 tariff lists $24 for international day visitors, $18 for SADC day visitors and $10 for a foreign-registered day-visitor car. The former $15/$7/$5 values were replaced.

ZimParks' 2026 tariff lists $24 international and $18 SADC daily conservation fees, with $10 for a foreign-registered day-visitor car. Permit and guide requirements remain an explicit confirmation step.
ZimParks' 2026 tariff lists $30 for international day visitors, $20 for SADC day visitors and $10 for a foreign-registered day-visitor car. Remote access remains subject to direct condition checks.

Gorongosa's official fees page lists $20 international and $10 SADC daily conservation fees, no vehicle conservation fee, gates from 06:00 to 18:00, and states that self-driving inside the park is not currently allowed.

ANAC confirms the park, contact details and 24-hour visiting access but does not publish a dependable current visitor tariff. The unsupported MT700 estimate was withdrawn; park and operator charges require confirmation.
ANAC confirms 06:00 to 17:00 daily visiting hours and park contacts but no dependable current public visitor tariff. The card now requires direct confirmation of park and boat charges.
Malawi's tourism authority confirms Liwonde and DNPW responsibility, but no dependable current public tariff was located. The former $25/$12/$5 figures were withdrawn.
Malawi's tourism authority confirms Nyika and DNPW responsibility, but no dependable current public tariff was located. The former entry, vehicle and camping estimates were withdrawn.

Malawi's tourism authority confirms Lake Malawi National Park and its visitor activities, but no dependable current public tariff was located. The former entry and snorkelling estimates were withdrawn.
Lesotho's Department of Environment confirms Sehlabathebe but publishes no dependable current visitor tariff or gate schedule. The former entry, vehicle and camping estimates were withdrawn.
Lesotho's Department of Environment confirms Ts'ehlanyane but publishes no dependable current visitor tariff or gate schedule. The former entry and camping estimates were withdrawn.
Lesotho's Department of Environment confirms Bokong Nature Reserve but publishes no dependable current visitor tariff or gate schedule. The former entry and camping estimates were withdrawn.
Big Game Parks lists a ZAR/E95 daily conservation fee, 06:00 to 18:00 day visits, half price for children under 13, and cashless payment from 1 July 2026. The old E250/E125/E50 table was removed.
Big Game Parks lists a ZAR/E95 daily conservation fee, 06:00 to 18:00 day visits, half price for children under 13, and cashless payment. The former E80/E40 values were corrected.

Malolotja is managed by the Eswatini National Trust Commission, not Big Game Parks. ENTC confirms 06:00 to 18:00 daily visiting hours but no dependable current tariff was captured, so the old E50/E25/E40 values were withdrawn.
South Africa's BMA and Namibia's published customs schedule both list Vioolsdrift / Noordoewer as a 24-hour crossing. The generic ministry link and unsupported fee range were replaced.
Martin's Drift and Groblersbrug are opposite sides of one crossing. BMA lists Groblersbrug at 08:00 to 22:00; the duplicate Groblersbrug card and unsupported 06:00 opening were removed.
BMA lists Beitbridge as a 24-hour port. The card no longer presents invented live-wait or numeric vehicle-fee ranges.

Kazungula Bridge directly joins Botswana and Zambia, not Zimbabwe. Botswana's April 2026 notice says the planned 24-hour rollout was stalled without a new date; Zambia's published schedule lists 06:00 to 18:00.

Zambia's official schedule lists Victoria Falls Border Control at 06:00 to 20:00. The crossing serves both pedestrians and vehicles, and the immigration authority confirms the passport-dependent KAZA and day-tripper facilities.

Namibia confirms Ngoma as an official land border and visa-on-arrival point but the reviewed authority pages do not publish dependable current passenger hours. The unsupported 06:00 to 18:00 claim was replaced with a direct-confirmation instruction.

Lebombo and Ressano Garcia are the two sides of one crossing. BMA publishes 06:00 to midnight on the South African side; Mozambique reports 24-hour Ressano Garcia operations, so the practical joint window uses the earlier close.
Both Lesotho Home Affairs and South Africa's BMA list Maseru Bridge as a 24-hour crossing. Unsupported wait and fee estimates were removed.
BMA lists Oshoek at 07:00 to 22:00 while Eswatini customs publishes later processing at Ngwenya. The card now uses the South African-side close as the safe practical limit.

Malawi Immigration confirms Mchinji borders Zambia's Mwami post; Zambia's statutory schedule lists Mwami for 24-hour operation. This replaces the geographically incorrect Nakonde / Tunduma Zambia–Malawi card.
Zambia's published statutory schedule lists Chirundu at 06:00 to 20:00, not 18:00. The unsupported KAZA reference, numeric fee range and live-wait estimate were removed.

ZIMRA confirms the Plumtree post and Botswana reporting identifies 06:00 to 22:00 normal staffing. Official notices show that 24-hour schedules have been temporary festive extensions, not normal hours.
Botswana and Namibia authority reporting confirms that Mamuno / Trans-Kalahari moved to round-the-clock operation in 2023. The former 06:00 to 22:00 hours were corrected.
SANParks confirms Pafuri is a South Africa–Mozambique border gate operating 08:00 to 16:00 year-round. The former South Africa–Zimbabwe pairing and unsupported four-night / 4x4 claims were removed.
Namibia's revenue and home-affairs reporting confirms that Katima Mulilo moved to 24-hour operation in August 2023. The obsolete ferry-or-bridge wording and 06:00 to 18:00 hours were replaced.
BMA confirms Kopfontein as a South African port but its current public hours table does not provide a dependable row. The unsupported 06:00 to 22:00 claim was replaced with direct confirmation.
BMA lists Skilpadshek at 06:00 to midnight. The card now names Botswana's Pioneer Gate side and removes the unsupported 22:00 close and numeric fee range.
South African BMA and Namibia customs both list Nakop / Ariamsvlei for 24-hour operation. The Namibia-side name and current visa-on-arrival context were added.
BMA lists Caledonspoort at 06:00 to 22:00 and Lesotho government notices confirm that it is not normally a 24-hour crossing. The misspelled ID and false 24-hour claim were corrected.
Lesotho Home Affairs lists Qacha's Nek at 07:00 to 20:00 while BMA lists the South African side later. The card uses the earlier Lesotho-side close as the practical limit.
SANParks confirms seasonal 08:00 to 16:00 / 15:00 hours, tourism-only status and the compulsory park overnight. Temporary flood closures are now identified as a same-day confirmation risk.
Eswatini's revenue service confirms Mhlumeni as a 24-hour customs post. This useful Eswatini–Mozambique crossing replaces the duplicate Komatipoort / Ressano Garcia card.
Current Eswatini government and revenue-service pages list Lomahasha at 07:00 to 20:00. The former 06:00 to 22:00 hours and unsupported vehicle-fee range were removed.
Malawi Immigration confirms that Mwanza, not Mchinji, is paired with Mozambique's Zóbuè post. No dependable current passenger hours were located, so the old hours and fee estimates were withdrawn.

Zimbabwe and Mozambique authority sources identify the crossing as Forbes / Machipanda. ZIMRA confirms round-the-clock operation since January 2024; the incorrect Mukumbura pairing and 06:00 to 18:00 hours were removed.
BMA lists Ramatlabama as a separate South Africa–Botswana crossing operating 06:00 to 22:00. It replaces the duplicate Groblersbrug record while preserving the collection's coverage count.

BMA and Mozambique's conservation authority both list Kosi Bay / Ponta do Ouro at 08:00 to 17:00. The universal 4x4 and tide-track claims were removed because the main surfaced approach has changed access assumptions.

Both Lesotho Home Affairs and BMA list Sani Pass at 06:00 to 18:00 normal hours. The unsupported 08:00 to 16:00 schedule and universal vehicle claim were replaced with a road-condition confirmation instruction.
South Africa's BMA and Eswatini's revenue service both list Golela / Lavumisa at 07:00 to 22:00. The unsupported 06:00 opening and numeric fee wording were removed.

Lesotho Home Affairs and BMA both identify Ficksburg Bridge / Maputsoe as a 24-hour crossing. Van Rooyen's Gate is separate, so the former combined name and misleading route description were corrected.
